correctness.rationale: For arbitrary continuous test functions of y and z, invariance of antiderivatives gives \(\mathbb E[(c-dx^2-y)\phi(y)]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[(s(x-x_R)-z)\psi(z)]=0\), proving the two conditional laws. Orthogonal conditional-residual decompositions give the two variance identities because the residuals are exactly \(-\dot y/d\) and \(\dot z/(rs)\). The mean parabola is the first/second-moment subtraction. If either speed square vanishes, support invariance makes the corresponding coordinate constant on each complete bounded support orbit and the remaining equations force an equilibrium; the mean-parabola equality is stricter and forces one equilibrium atom. The exact checker independently verifies all load-bearing polynomial residual identities.

value.rationale: The two recovery nullclines are central structural objects in a canonical neuron model. Identifying them as exact stationary regression laws and quantifying their residual fluctuations by physical coordinate speeds yields reusable constraints for periodic, chaotic, or mixed recurrent states and a precise equilibrium-rigidity test; this is more informative than a numerical moment estimate.

final_claim: For the canonical three-dimensional Hindmarsh--Rose flow with \(d,r,s>0\), every compactly supported invariant probability measure satisfies \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid y]=(c-y)/d\) and \(\mathbb E[x\mid z]=x_R+z/s\), the stated mean-parabola defect, and the exact variance--speed identities \(d^2\operatorname{Var}(x^2)-\operatorname{Var}(y)=\mathbb E[\dot y^2]\) and \(s^2\operatorname{Var}(x)-\operatorname{Var}(z)=r^{-2}\mathbb E[\dot z^2]\), with the stated equilibrium rigidity.
limitations: Compactly supported invariant probabilities only; existence or uniqueness of a non-equilibrium invariant measure is not asserted.
The identities constrain selected conditional first moments and variances rather than determining firing statistics or the full invariant law.
